Incorporating SLOOS signals, credit supply looks more supportive than the FSR alone suggested. Banks have eased standards across key consumer categories (credit cards, auto, and other consumer loans) and in residential real estate, including lower minimum credit score requirements and easier HELOC and GSE-eligible mortgage standards. Large banks have eased for investment-grade firms, though C&I policies remain tighter for riskier borrowers, and foreign banks report tighter standards for below-investment-grade firms while holding steady for investment grade. Net takeaway: credit availability is improving broadly, reinforcing accommodative financial conditions cited by the FOMC, but remains uneven for lower-rated borrowers. This nudges the assessment modestly more positive than the prior FSR-based view, while preserving caution around risk-tier segmentation.
